lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: C.J. Stroud throws for 3 TDs as the Texans roll past the Colts 26-3
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: J.  Stroud had another big game to help the Houston Texans finally get a victory at home.  Stroud threw for 194 yards and three touchdowns and the Texans used a strong defensive performance to coast to a 26-3 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night.  With the roof at Reliant Stadium open for the first time since 2024, the Texans won a home game for the first time this season after losing their first four.
lastCompletedGameRecap.upNextNotes: Up next Colts: Host the New York Giants on Nov. 29. Texans: Host Baltimore on Nov. 29.

irReserve.name: Greg Newsome II
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: Newsome is expected to undergo surgery for a sprained ankle that he sustained in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. Now that he's on IR, Newsome will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Lions on Monday, Dec. 28. Paulson Adebo is expected to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside cornerback in Newsome's absence.

irReserve.name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

coachingMatchup.headline: Shane Steichen & DC Lou Anarumo vs. HC John Harbaugh, OC Matt Nagy & DC Dennard Wilson (Lucas Oil Stadium)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Indianapolis Colts's staff (Shane Steichen, OC Jim Bob Cooter, DC Lou Anarumo) against New York Giants (6-3-1)—testing both Indianapolis's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Shane Steichen and OC Jim Bob Cooter pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress New York Giants's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against New York Giants's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Lou Anarumo balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Indianapolis sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to New York Giants's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: Lucas Oil Stadium situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Anthony Richardson Sr., Tyler Warren & Laquon Treadwell vs. CB Deonte Banks & LB Kayvon Thibodeaux
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: IND: #30 Pass Off (163.3 yds) · #31 Off. Scoring (-6.81) | NYG: #8 Pass Def (-1.28)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Anthony Richardson Sr., Tyler Warren & Laquon Treadwell attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against New York Giants's #8 pass defense (-1.28). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Indianapolis's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Anthony Richardson Sr. (#5) scanning Giants's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Kayvon Thibodeaux widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Tyler Warren (#84).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Laiatu Latu, Jaylahn Tuimoloau & Grover Stewart vs. QB J.J. McCarthy & OT Andrew Thomas
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: IND: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | NYG: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Laiatu Latu, Jaylahn Tuimoloau & Grover Stewart lead Indianapolis's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against New York Giants's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Colts keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Laiatu Latu (#97) draw chip help from Giants's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Jaylahn Tuimoloau (#91).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Cam Bynum, Charvarius Ward & Sauce Gardner vs. WR Malik Nabers & QB J.J. McCarthy
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: IND: #17 Pass Def (+1.92) | NYG: #15 Pass Off (221.2 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Cam Bynum, Charvarius Ward & Sauce Gardner anchor Indianapolis's #17 pass defense (+1.92) against WR Malik Nabers and New York Giants's #15 passing attack (221.2 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Giants into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Cam Bynum (#0) at the top of routes against WR Malik Nabers: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB J.J. McCarthy's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Jonathan Taylor & Ashton Dulin vs. Giants Front Seven & LB Kayvon Thibodeaux
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: IND: #15 Rush Off (113.4 yds) | NYG: #25 Rush Def (+0.08)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Jonathan Taylor & Ashton Dulin test New York Giants's #25 run defense (+0.08) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Giants's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Giants's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Jonathan Taylor (#28).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Matt Goncalves, Tanor Bortolini & Jalen Travis vs. DT Shelby Harris & Giants Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: IND: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | NYG: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Matt Goncalves, Tanor Bortolini & Jalen Travis protect Anthony Richardson Sr. (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DT Shelby Harris and New York Giants's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Matt Goncalves (#71) on obvious passing downs—if DT Shelby Harris cannot win clean around the arc, Giants must dial up interior stunts that stress Tanor Bortolini (#60).
